function: Learned CSIT acquisition: CNN-based distributed compression of LS sensing-channel estimates at secondary APs and joint aggregation/denoising at the CPU for reciprocity calibration under limited feedback (pp. 6-8)
system: Cell-free massive MIMO ISAC, TDD: M=5 APs with N=32-antenna ULAs, single-antenna UEs, point targets; 2.4 GHz carrier, 200 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (pp. 3, 9)
method: Per-AP CNN plus FC compression and CPU FC plus DnCNN aggregation; offline SGD training called unsupervised, with noisy LS estimates as labels instead of clean labels (pp. 7-9)
data_channel: Own Monte-Carlo simulation: extended Saleh-Valenzuela communication channel and scatter sensing channel, 3GPP urban microcell NLoS path loss only, 19200 training and 6400 test instances (pp. 3, 9)
test_conditions: Held-out 6400 test instances from the same Monte-Carlo set as 19200 training instances; sweeps of power, AP count, compression rate and training size; no unseen scenario (pp. 9-12)
baselines: Non-learned: Argos, dot-division (DD), LS calibration, with PCA compression, no calibration. Own variants: fully collaborated, fully non-collaborated, without CNN, without DnCNN, Restormer (pp. 9-12)
metrics: NMSE of calibrated CSIT; sum-rate of conjugate beamforming with calibrated downlink channels (pp. 9-12)
complexity: Order O(M N^2) for the proposed method versus O((MN)^3) for DD and LS (p. 10); Restormer variant over 100 times more FLOPs (p. 13)
q1_support: p. 3: "we adopt the extended Saleh-Valenzuela geometric model [30]"; p. 9: "PLml follows the 3GPP NLoS Urban Microcell path loss model [42, Table B.1.2.1-1]". Custom Monte-Carlo simulator with only the path loss from 3GPP; no 38.901, CDL/TDL, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "19200 instances for training and 6400 instances for testing", generated by the same Monte-Carlo simulation; Figs. 4-6, 8, 9 sweep power, number of APs, feedback rate, training size and depth. Missing: a trained model tested on another scenario, number of APs, band or site, or any reported adaptation.
q3_support: p. 9: "comparing it with the conventional calibration methods such as Argos [10], dot-division (DD) [40], and LS [15], [16] calibration methods as baseline approaches" (non-learned, NMSE). Learned comparisons are variants of the proposed structure: p. 10: "the same structure is adopted as previously introduced in Section IV-B for fair comparison"; p. 12: ablations remove the CNN or DnCNN module. Missing: an earlier learned calibration method or a standalone standard network.
q4_support: p. 10: "our DSC-based method is primarily dominated by network processing, scaling as O(M N 2 )", against O((M N)^3) for DD and LS; p. 13: Restormer variant has "over 100 times higher computation complexity in terms of floating-point operations".
q5_support: p. 9: "Monte-Carlo simulations are performed to generate the dataset"; the data are the authors' own simulation, and no link, DOI or public dataset of channels is given for code or data.
notes: Area 2: the learned networks compress LS estimates of the sensing channel for limited feedback and recover and denoise the CSIT at the CPU (pp. 6-8), with NMSE of the CSIT as main metric; reciprocity calibration is counted here as CSIT acquisition, so the reviewer should confirm that it falls under channel estimation and feedback. q3 is 0 because the fully collaborated, fully non-collaborated, ablated and Restormer comparisons are variants of the proposed framework (pp. 10, 12), and Argos, DD and LS are not learned; the authors' earlier learned calibration [19] is cited on p. 2 but not compared. The introduction ties the fully non-collaborated scheme to CSI compression schemes [29] (p. 2), but the experiments implement it with the proposed structure (p. 10), so it is treated as a variant. q1 is 0 because only the path loss comes from 3GPP.
